sources.place_summary: Cobb Mountain Art & Ecology Project (CMAEP) in Middletown, CA has six to ten wood-firing workshops per year plus soda and other atmospheric firing workshops. It offers three residency types (long-term, short-term, and wood-fire specialist) with access to an anagama, train, cross-draft, and gas kilns, and provides a firing membership for regular workshop participants.

sources.notes: Found one dated workshop with firing component ("Safe Stokes" - a wood firing workshop, sold out, Oct 19-23, 2026) and one residency with multiple firing types. The other workshops listed (Gestural Vessels, Littoral Landscapes, etc.) are forming/altering classes without mention of firing. Pages mention a ceramics residency with wood and soda kilns available.
sources.place_summary: Mendocino Art Center has ceramic studios with electric, gas, wood (train kiln), and wood/soda (catenary arch) kilns. The center offers a ceramics residency program (October-May annually) and occasional firing workshops announced on their workshops page.

sources.notes: The pages show one current firing opportunity: a 12-week wood firing workshop scheduled September 3–November 19, 2026 (dates within the 12-month window). Registration is closed as of the search date (2026-10-04), shown by "Sales ended" on the Eventbrite page. The workshop is offered through Laney College as a class enrollment opportunity for students. Past workshops (wood kiln building and inaugural firing in August 2025, and various non-firing workshops) are not recorded per instructions. The academic calendar and general events pages do not list additional firing opportunities beyond this workshop.
sources.place_summary: Laney College Ceramics has a wood-fired train kiln used for instruction. The college offers wood firing workshops through its Art Department; interested potters should contact the Art Department Chair or monitor the Laney events and workshops page for upcoming class announcements.

sources.notes: The pages describe wheel-throwing classes and handbuilding workshops but do not mention firing, kilns, or specific firing types for the classes themselves (e.g., 'Pottery on the Wheel; All Levels', 'Pinching Big', 'Handbuilding: Here Comes the Holidays'). Per instructions, classes without stated firing components are excluded. Three ongoing ways in qualify: Full Studio Membership and Home Studio Membership (both offering ongoing access to soda, raku, gas, and electric kilns) and a 6-month Artist Residency program. All three are open to potters beyond the studio electric kiln.
sources.place_summary: Sonoma Community Center's ceramics program offers open studio access and memberships with soda, raku, gas, and electric kilns for potters beyond the wheel-throwing stage. Outside potters can join via membership (with prior experience or after taking a class) or apply for 6-month artist residencies; the site announces classes and firings via its website calendar and email newsletter.

sources.place_summary: Uncle Paul's Ceramics operates two studios in San Francisco (Haight Street and North Beach) and partners with Oribe Firing Center in San Gregorio for soda firings. The studio offers wheel-throwing and handbuilding classes, memberships with kiln access, and workshops including soda firing experiences; firing announcements appear on their website and through platforms like Mato.

sources.place_summary: Mendocino College has a fully equipped ceramics studio with 5 electric kilns, 4 gas reduction kilns, 1 raku kiln, 1 saggar setup, and a soda kiln, plus 18 pottery wheels. The college offers Associate Degree and Master Technician Certificate programs in ceramics to students; outside potters should contact the college directly about community access and firing opportunities.
